s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis
salient_findings: Recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb
key_facts: 56-year-old man
Four-year history of skin lesion on the right thumb
Partial amputation of the thumb in December 2016
Lesion reappeared at the distal aspect of the thumb stump in August 2017
No significant medical history
No medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion over the dorsum of the right thumb stump
Lesion is mobile over deep structures
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Metastatic workup included CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis and a bone scan
Enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer with potential for local recurrence

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer with high risk of metastasis

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant skin cancer with potential for metastasis and poor prognosis

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Locally aggressive skin cancer with potential for recurrence

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant skin cancer with potential for metastasis and association with immunosuppression

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare and aggressive skin cancer with high risk of metastasis

shortlist.label: Epithelioid sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare and aggressive skin cancer with potential for metastasis and poor prognosis

raw.rationale: The lesion's recurrence after partial amputation and the presence of an enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node suggest an aggressive skin cancer, which is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma than other options like basal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely to metastasize and recur aggressively

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more rapid growth rate and is more likely to be associated with immunosuppression

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: Usually pigmented and has a different set of risk factors and clinical behaviors

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Characterized by a distinctive histological appearance and typically has a slower growth rate

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Strongly associated with immunosuppression and has a distinct clinical and histological appearance

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more rapid growth rate and is often associated with lymphedema

rejected.label: Epithelioid sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in younger individuals and has a distinct clinical and histological appearance
